name: Private credit stress
value: BDC tenders above 5% caps; ASIC flags gaps
summary: Redemption limits at large private credit funds persist; Australia's ASIC flags weak disclosure on 10 Nov
state: Redemption requests at large US non-traded BDCs have exceeded 5% quarterly caps for several quarters, with many funds prorating payouts in Q3 (Crowdfunded Wealth tracker). On 10 Nov Australia's regulator ASIC said complex structures and poor disclosure persist in the sector, noting six interim stop orders and redemption limits at lender CVS Lane (ABC News). This run found no forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers as of 10 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Investors in private credit funds may not be able to withdraw money when they want, as quarterly limits apply. Wider spillovers to banks or insurers have not been seen.
rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions (Watch); no simultaneous gating wave or bank/insurer losses (Alert)

sources.title: ABC News — ASIC slams $250 billion private credit sector as risks to investors remain
Crowdfunded Wealth — Private credit fund redemptions tracker, October 2026

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
